entries.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: existing Sichuan countryside narrative game postcard, strong cleanup of excessive surface texture.
Input: Image 1 is the ONLY input and ONLY full-image edit target, the latest TREE-VIEW illustration. Preserve this exact high-angle camera and composition. This is NOT a redesign.
User request: the picture is much too mottled and busy, particularly the innumerable leaf-shaped shadows on the ground and branch, the chopped-up bark scales and random ground flecks. REPAINT these surfaces into clean coherent hand-painted color planes. The difference must be immediately obvious at thumbnail size and when looking closely. Remove nearly all unnecessary high-frequency dappled marks rather than making a subtle reduction.
Highest priority 1 — CAST SHADOWS: remove the carpet of tiny disconnected leaf silhouettes and tiny bright holes across the courtyard, branch/trunk, walls and furniture. Replace the dappled pattern with only a FEW large continuous softly bounded areas of tree shade and open sunlight. No recognizable confetti-sized leaf-shaped shadows scattered across the floor or branch. Keep the warm daylight direction and natural contact shadows under chairs, feet, objects and the toad so nothing floats. Do not leave the courtyard completely flat white.
Highest priority 2 — TREE BARK: repaint the big foreground branch and left trunk with one warm brown base, one broad deeper-brown underside shadow and one restrained broad upper light plane. Keep the branch silhouette, fork, curvature and volume. Show only a FEW long flowing structural bark grooves following the branch. Remove the hundreds of tiny gray/brown chips, scales, tiles, broken rectangles, black crevice specks and spotted sunlight. It must read as an organic tree branch, not brickwork, camouflage, pebbles or a mosaic.
Highest priority 3 — GROUND: large calm intact base-color areas, no dense little golden/gray/cream paint chips, patchwork or grain. Preserve the correct ground material and any essential perspective seams; use at most a few broad low-amplitude tonal variations, never little flecks. Leave substantial quiet breathing space around people and furniture.
Related foliage and surfaces: retain the actual leaf silhouettes and botanical forms, but each foreground leaf should have one coherent main green color and at most one simple shadow plane; no little highlight chips. Merge shrub and distant greenery interiors into larger connected clumps. Keep existing flowers as flowers, not new decoration. Bamboo, walls, roof tiles and clothing may retain necessary joints/folds/outlines but not extra mottled surface noise.
Absolute locks: retain exact framing, perspective, object count, all object and character positions and scales, story action, individual silhouettes and relationships. ONE toad and ONE bag on the SAME foreground branch in the SAME pose looking down, same olive body, amber eye, orange glands, cream belly edge, short legs, warm brown outline and larger identifying wart marks. Its important wart markings are not the unwanted background speckles. Same indigo white-flower bag, brass clasp and red chili knot. Do not remove the satchel flower or make the toad unrecognizably smooth.
Style: still warm soft 2D hand-painted gouache with gently imperfect edges and very sparse brush variation, original palette and depth. Clean color planes, NOT plastic airbrush or vector art. No Gaussian blur, soft-focus cleanup, smearing, bleaching, desaturation or lowering contrast to conceal the marks. Do not replace the removed texture with paper grain, stippling, noise or new crosshatching. No new props, labels, captions, borders or watermarks. Full opaque native1536x1024 landscape3:2.
Scene-specific locks: retain the two human men at center-right — cream-shirt reclining customer and gray-blue-shirt practitioner performing ear cleaning. Keep their faces, hand/tool gesture, bamboo reclining chair, side table, folded towel, dark tool roll and gaiwan unchanged. Toad stays on the tree watching them, never becomes the ear-cleaning customer. Keep tiled teahouse at left and surrounding empty bamboo tables/chairs/umbrellas. The courtyard MUST stay gray paving: preserve broad slab outlines, perspective seams and a few coherent green moss strips between slabs, but make each slab's face plain quiet warm-gray rather than a dense field of leaf-shadow puzzle pieces. Most important: completely simplify the many overlapping tiny leaf shadows in the large central paving region, and the heavily chipped foreground branch beneath the toad and bag. Do not alter the composition to hide the difficult regions. No text.
